title: The Crab Derby, 2007
logline: Twenty-third annual. A tourist offers Gully a hundred dollars for the 1998 flyer. Gully says it's not for sale. Wood hears it from the stool.

panels.composition: Gully's. A TOURIST pointing at the wall of flyers, the oldest one, 1998, weathered. GULLY. WOOD on the stool, normal size, drawing this year's on the counter.

balloons.text: The first one. The '98. A hundred bucks.

image.prompt: a tourist pointing at the oldest of a row of crab flyers on a shingle wall, a man in an apron behind the counter, a thin man on a stool drawing, a dog, muddy flats

balloons.text: It was twenty. It's still twenty. Nobody's paid it but me.

image.prompt: close-up of a stocky man in an apron, flat and final

panels.composition: Wood on the stool, having heard. Not looking up. The new crab under his pen. Two crabs, a cup, and this year — a third, very small crab, in the corner, facing the first.

image.prompt: close-up of a hand drawing a crab flyer with two large crabs, a cup, and a very small third crab in the corner

panels.composition: Thirteen flyers. Gully pinning. The tourist gone. The twenty on the counter. Wood not taking it yet.

characters.pose: the twenty on the counter between them

image.prompt: thirteen crab flyers in a row, a man in an apron pinning the newest, a twenty-dollar bill lying on the counter between him and a thin man on a stool, no words

art.line: brush-pen scanned; muddy digital flats; Sundays in watercolor, improving
art.palette: limited, muddy; Sundays gray-green, rust, one warm

notes: Two hundred dollars refused. The third small crab: the tourist, maybe. The strip doesn't say.
